steps.title: Why loops exist
steps.content: A loop repeats a block of code. Use a for loop when iterating over a known sequence or range. Use a while loop when repetition depends on a condition.
steps.example: for i in range(3): print(i) prints 0, 1, 2.
steps.tip: Before tracing a loop, write the initial value, condition and update.

steps.title: Trace a for loop
steps.prompt: What does for i in range(1, 4): print(i) print?
steps.explanation: In Python, range(1,4) includes 1 and stops before 4: 1, 2, 3.

steps.title: Understand while loops
steps.content: A while loop checks its condition before each iteration. The loop body must eventually change something that makes the condition false, or it can run forever.
steps.example: n=3; while n>0: print(n); n-=1 prints 3,2,1 and stops.
steps.tip: Check that every loop has a reachable exit condition.

steps.title: Count iterations
steps.prompt: x starts at 2. While x < 10, add 2 to x. How many times does the loop body run?
steps.explanation: x values at the start are 2,4,6,8. Four iterations; then x becomes 10 and the condition is false.

steps.title: Break, continue and nested loops
steps.content: break exits the nearest loop. continue skips the rest of the current iteration. A nested loop runs the inner loop for each outer iteration; n×m iterations when the bounds are fixed.
steps.example: Two loops each running 3 times produce 3×3 = 9 inner executions.

questions.prompt: In Python, how many values are generated by range(5)?
What is the purpose of break?
questions.explanation: break exits the nearest enclosing loop immediately.

questions.prompt: How many times does this run: for i in range(2): for j in range(3): print(i,j)?
questions.explanation: Two outer iterations, each with three inner iterations: 2×3 = 6.

questions.prompt: When is a while loop usually appropriate?
options: Only when the count is exactly 10
questions.explanation: A while loop continues while its condition is true.

options: The loop condition never becomes false
questions.explanation: If the condition remains true forever, the loop never exits.
